$comment: Lighthouse CI budgets for DiScammer (Task Q2). Pin: @lhci/cli@0.15.1.
Run via scripts/lhci.sh (resolves Chrome + lets BASE_URL override the urls below).
FLOORS ARE A RATCHET: set slightly BELOW the current measured category
scores so the gate can only hold or improve. Measured 2026-06 against the
uvicorn DEV server (median of 3 runs) — dockerized prod (nginx gzip +
caching, baked static) scores HIGHER, so these dev-derived floors are
conservative. Re-measure with scripts/lhci.sh and RAISE floors when the
numbers durably climb. See docs/deploy/visual-regression.md (Q2 section).
Measured dev medians (perf/a11y/bp/seo, TBTms, CLS):
/en/inspect        84/100/100/100  TBT 0    CLS 0.125
/en/guide/phishing 88/ 96/100/100  TBT 0    CLS 0.000
(a cold first run of /en/ once measured perf 69 / TBT 175ms — the ceilings
below absorb that cold-start jitter so the gate doesn't flake.)
CI NOTE: `performance` + `total-blocking-time` are `warn`, NOT `error`.
Lighthouse perf on a shared GitHub runner is CPU-contended and meaningless
(first CI run measured perf 0.59 / TBT 6445ms vs 80-88 / 0ms on a dev box).
We gate HARD on the deterministic categories (a11y / best-practices / seo /
CLS) and only REPORT perf/TBT so a noisy runner can't block a deploy. Track
perf via the uploaded report / a real environment, not this CI gate.
